result.note: Tests the elevation to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, the 2030 trade target and PTA status, the UPI–UZQR payment link, and uranium and trade figures.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–Uzbekistan summit held in August 2026:
items: The two countries elevated their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
The two countries set a bilateral trade target of USD 5 billion by 2030.
Negotiations on a Preferential Trade Agreement began after a feasibility study was completed.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: A feasibility study has been completed and could lead to a Preferential Trade Agreement, but negotiations have not begun. The USD 5 billion target for 2030 compares with trade of USD 1.3 billion and needs roughly 31 per cent annual growth for five years.
questions.source: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev elevated ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership on Sunday and reported progress on a long-term uranium supply arrangement.

questions.prompt: Under an agreement signed between India and Uzbekistan in August 2026, Indian Unified Payments Interface (UPI) apps will be able to scan which payment codes?
questions.explain: The agreement allows Indian UPI apps to scan Uzbekistan's UZQR payment codes. It was one of 11 instruments signed, alongside deals on mineral resources and financial dialogue.
questions.source: Among 11 signed instruments were deals on mineral resources and financial dialogue, plus an agreement allowing Indian Unified Payments Interface apps to scan Uzbekistan’s UZQR payment codes.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India–Uzbekistan economic ties, as reported in August 2026:
items: 2019 uranium supply contract — 1,100 metric tonnes through 2026
Uzbekistan's imports from India — USD 164.6 million
Growth in bilateral trade in 2025 — 33.3 per cent
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: Uzbekistan imported USD 1.15 billion from India; USD 164.6 million is the value of its exports to India, which makes trade lopsided. The latest talks point to a successor uranium arrangement but disclosed no quantity, price or timetable.
questions.source: A 2019 contract already covers 1,100 metric tonnes of Uzbek uranium through 2026.
